frk_001: You can recognise it by standing right on the public street, the subway line beneath it curved to spare it. It stands on Eschersheimer Landstraße, at Lindenbaum station.
frk_002: You can recognise it by its soft, feathery needles turning rust orange and dropping entirely each autumn, unlike an evergreen conifer. It stands in the East Asia section of the Botanical Garden.
frk_003: You can recognise it by its drooping branches rooted where they touch the ground, forming a hollow green room you can walk into. It stands west of the Palmenhaus, by the Gesellschaftshaus.
frk_004: You can recognise it by its low, wide crown standing alone on open meadow, leaves opening translucent red before darkening to black-purple. It stands in the middle of the Palmengarten.
frk_005: You can recognise it by its eight trunks rising in one tight ring from a single planting, hollow enough to stand inside. It stands at a path crossing in the middle of Grüneburgpark.
frk_006: You can recognise it by its trunk, 7.13 metres round, standing directly behind the neoclassical Nebbiensches Gartenhaus. It stands in the Bockenheimer Anlage.
